title: Factorized object/style Mirror codes for held-out function combinations
hypothesis: On a 4-object x 4-style continuous function grid with four diagonal pairs fully held out, factorized Mirror codes achieve held-out-pair normalized RMSE <=1.1x factorized latent codes while using <=1.1x their actual bytes and beat direct pair-code views by >=10% RMSE.
mirror_coordinate: one learned Givens angle per object and per style, composed on separate hidden planes
logical_multiplicity: 16 object/style functions represented by factor combinations
controls: direct per-pair Mirror angle table with held-out entries untrained
independent per-pair decoder oracle trained on all pairs

task.teacher: shared coordinate MLP with object and style disjoint Givens views

development.selection_metric: lowest validation normalized RMSE on observed pairs only

success_gate: On each fresh world, Mirror held-out-pair normalized RMSE <=1.1x factorized latent and Mirror bytes <=1.1x latent bytes, with >=10% lower RMSE than direct pair-code Mirror table.
failure_gate: Mirror misses any held-out quality or byte threshold, or a simple factorized control dominates at similar bytes.
boundaries: Teacher generated from the same compositional Givens family; aligned feasibility only.
Diagonal pairs are unseen during training/validation for non-oracle methods.
No natural object/style or 3D reconstruction claim.
